claim: Ciliary G-protein Rab28 is associated with human autosomal recessive cone-rod dystrophy.
source: Here, we show that the ciliary G-protein Rab28, associated with human autosomal recessive cone-rod dystrophy, negatively regulates EV levels in the sensory organs of Caenorhabditis elegans in a cilia specific manner.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations to human genetic studies (Roosing et al., 2013; Riveiro-Álvarez et al., 2015; Lee et al., 2017) in the introduction.

claim: Rab28 negatively regulates EV levels in the sensory organs of Caenorhabditis elegans in a cilia specific manner.
source: Here, we show that the ciliary G-protein Rab28, associated with human autosomal recessive cone-rod dystrophy, negatively regulates EV levels in the sensory organs of Caenorhabditis elegans in a cilia specific manner.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data showing EV accumulation in rab-28 mutants as shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: Sequential targeting of lipidated Rab28 to periciliary and ciliary membranes is highly dependent on the BBSome.
source: Sequential targeting of lipidated Rab28 to periciliary and ciliary membranes is highly dependent on the BBSome and the prenyl-binding protein phosphodiesterase 6 subunit delta (PDE6D), respectively, and BBSome loss causes excessive and ectopic EV production.
evidence: This is supported by localization data in Figures 1 and 2 showing RAB-28 mislocalization in BBSome mutants.

claim: Sequential targeting of lipidated Rab28 to periciliary and ciliary membranes is highly dependent on the prenyl-binding protein phosphodiesterase 6 subunit delta (PDE6D).
source: Sequential targeting of lipidated Rab28 to periciliary and ciliary membranes is highly dependent on the BBSome and the prenyl-binding protein phosphodiesterase 6 subunit delta (PDE6D), respectively, and BBSome loss causes excessive and ectopic EV production.
evidence: This is supported by localization data in Figures 1 and 2 showing RAB-28 IFT defects in pdl-1 mutants.

claim: BBSome loss causes excessive and ectopic EV production.
source: Sequential targeting of lipidated Rab28 to periciliary and ciliary membranes is highly dependent on the BBSome and the prenyl-binding protein phosphodiesterase 6 subunit delta (PDE6D), respectively, and BBSome loss causes excessive and ectopic EV production.
evidence: This is supported by TEM data in Figures 5 and 6 showing EV accumulation in bbs-8 mutants.

claim: EV defective mutants display abnormalities in sensory compartment morphogenesis.
source: We also find that EV defective mutants display abnormalities in sensory compartment morphogenesis.
evidence: This is supported by TEM data in Figure 3 showing enlarged amphid compartments in bbs-8 and bbs-5 mutants.

claim: Rab28 and the BBSome are key in vivo regulators of EV production at the periciliary membrane.
source: Together, these findings reveal that Rab28 and the BBSome are key in vivo regulators of EV production at the periciliary membrane and suggest that EVs may mediate signaling between cilia and glia to shape sensory organ compartments.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing EV accumulation and localization patterns in mutants.

claim: EVs may mediate signaling between cilia and glia to shape sensory organ compartments.
source: Together, these findings reveal that Rab28 and the BBSome are key in vivo regulators of EV production at the periciliary membrane and suggest that EVs may mediate signaling between cilia and glia to shape sensory organ compartments.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the correlation between EV defects and sensory organ morphology defects.

claim: Defects in the biogenesis of cilia-related EVs may contribute to human ciliopathies.
source: Our data also suggest that defects in the biogenesis of cilia-related EVs may contribute to human ciliopathies.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the association of RAB28 with human disease and the EV phenotypes observed in C. elegans.

claim: Cilia are conserved microtubule (MT)-based organelles that extend from the surfaces of most eukaryotic cell types.
source: Cilia are conserved microtubule (MT)-based organelles that extend from the surfaces of most eukaryotic cell types.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about cilia structure.

claim: Cilia serve a variety of functions that include motility and signal transduction, as well as the capacity to shed extracellular vesicles (EV).
source: Cilia serve a variety of functions that include motility and signal transduction, as well as the capacity to shed extracellular vesicles (EV) (Wang and Barr, 2018; Carter and Blacque, 2019; Nachury and Mick, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to review articles on ciliary function.

claim: Defects in primary cilia lead to monosymptomatic and syndromic human disorders, collectively termed ciliopathies.
source: Defects in primary cilia lead to monosymptomatic and syndromic human disorders, collectively termed ciliopathies.
evidence: This is established knowledge about ciliopathies supported by citation (Waters and Beales, 2011).

claim: Ciliopathies include diseases such as autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD), retinitis pigmentosa, cone-rod dystrophy and Bardet-Biedl syndrome (BBS).
source: These include diseases such as autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD), retinitis pigmentosa, cone-rod dystrophy and Bardet-Biedl syndrome (BBS) (Waters and Beales, 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge about specific ciliopathies supported by citation.

claim: Intraflagellar transport (IFT) is driven by kinesin-II anterograde (ciliary base to tip) and cytoplasmic dynein 2 retrograde (ciliary tip to base) motors.
source: Intraflagellar transport (IFT) is driven by kinesin-II anterograde (ciliary base to tip) and cytoplasmic dynein 2 retrograde (ciliary tip to base) motors (Rosenbaum and Witman, 2002).
evidence: This is established knowledge about IFT mechanisms supported by citation.

claim: The BBSome regulates ciliary signaling cascades by removing various membrane proteins from cilia via retrograde IFT.
source: The BBSome regulates ciliary signaling cascades by removing various membrane proteins from cilia via retrograde IFT (Lechtreck et al., 2009; Liu and Lechtreck, 2018; Ye et al., 2018) and consists of an octameric complex (BBS1/2/4/5/7/8/9 and BBS18) that is recruited to membranes by the small G-protein Arl6 (Liew et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge about BBSome function supported by multiple citations.

claim: The BBSome consists of an octameric complex (BBS1/2/4/5/7/8/9 and BBS18) that is recruited to membranes by the small G-protein Arl6.
source: The BBSome regulates ciliary signaling cascades by removing various membrane proteins from cilia via retrograde IFT (Lechtreck et al., 2009; Liu and Lechtreck, 2018; Ye et al., 2018) and consists of an octameric complex (BBS1/2/4/5/7/8/9 and BBS18) that is recruited to membranes by the small G-protein Arl6 (Liew et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge about BBSome composition supported by citation.

claim: Most EV studies have used cultured cells or biofluids.
source: Most EV studies have used cultured cells or biofluids, and much effort has been invested in improving methodology for isolating and characterizing different EV subtypes using protein and lipid markers.
evidence: This is a general statement about the state of the EV field.

claim: Exosomes (30–150 nm in diameter) are generated through fusion of multivesicular bodies.
source: Exosomes (30–150 nm in diameter) are generated through fusion of multivesicular bodies. Microvesicles or ectosomes (100–1000 nm) bud from the plasma membrane (Maas et al., 2017; Raposo and Stoorvogel, 2013; Meldolesi, 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge about EV biogenesis supported by citations.

claim: Microvesicles or ectosomes (100–1000 nm) bud from the plasma membrane.
source: Exosomes (30–150 nm in diameter) are generated through fusion of multivesicular bodies. Microvesicles or ectosomes (100–1000 nm) bud from the plasma membrane (Maas et al., 2017; Raposo and Stoorvogel, 2013; Meldolesi, 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge about EV biogenesis supported by citations.

claim: EVs released from the tips of cilia are clearly ectosomal in origin.
source: EVs released from the tips of cilia are clearly ectosomal in origin (Wood et al., 2013; Phua et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies on ciliary EVs.

claim: C. elegans nematode is an excellent in vivo system to study ciliary formation, specialization, and function including EV shedding.
source: The C. elegans nematode is an excellent in vivo system to study ciliary formation, specialization, and function including EV shedding (Bargmann, 2006).
evidence: This is a statement about the utility of C. elegans as a model system supported by citation.

claim: Of the 302 neurons that comprise the hermaphrodite nervous system, 60 are ciliated.
source: Of the 302 neurons that comprise the hermaphrodite nervous system, 60 are ciliated (Ward et al., 1975; Perkins et al., 1986; Doroquez et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge about C. elegans supported by citations.

claim: C. elegans males possess an additional 54 ciliated neurons.
source: C. elegans males possess an additional 54 ciliated neurons (Sulston et al., 1980; Cook et al., 2019; Molina-García et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge about C. elegans males supported by citations.

claim: The cephalic male (CEM) and shared inner labial (IL2) neurons are the only known ciliated EV-releasing neurons (EVNs) as defined by imaging of fluorescently-tagged EV cargos released outside the animal.
source: The cephalic male (CEM) and shared inner labial (IL2) neurons are the only known ciliated EV-releasing neurons (EVNs) as defined by imaging of fluorescently-tagged EV cargos released outside the animal (Wang et al., 2014a).
evidence: This is a statement based on previous work from the authors' lab supported by citation.

claim: In C. elegans, EVs are 'shed' at the ciliary base and retained within lumens of the cephalic and inner labial sensory organs as visualized by transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and tomography reconstructions.
source: In C. elegans, EVs are 'shed' at the ciliary base and retained within lumens of the cephalic and inner labial sensory organs as visualized by transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and tomography reconstructions.
evidence: This is based on previous TEM observations from the authors' work.

claim: EVs are also 'released' from cilia directly into the environment outside of the sensory organs, as observed by fluorescently-tagged EV cargos such as the TRP polycystin PKD-2::GFP and myristoylated peripheral membrane protein CIL-7.
source: EVs are also 'released' from cilia directly into the environment outside of the sensory organs, as observed by fluorescently-tagged EV cargos such as the TRP polycystin PKD-2::GFP and myristoylated peripheral membrane protein CIL-7 (Wang et al., 2014a; Maguire et al., 2015).
evidence: This is based on previous fluorescence microscopy observations supported by citations.

claim: In C. elegans amphid and phasmid cilia, RAB-28 is a BBS-8-dependent IFT cargo that associates with the periciliary membrane (PCM) when in a GTP-bound conformation.
source: In C. elegans amphid and phasmid cilia, RAB-28 is a BBS-8-dependent IFT cargo that associates with the periciliary membrane (PCM) when in a GTP-bound conformation (Jensen et al., 2016).
evidence: This is based on previous work from the authors' lab supported by citation.

claim: C. elegans RAB-28 disruption leads to defects in amphid sensory compartment size via a proposed cell non-autonomous mechanism, previously speculated to involve EVs.
source: Functionally, C. elegans RAB-28 disruption leads to defects in amphid sensory compartment size via a proposed cell non-autonomous mechanism, previously speculated to involve EVs (Jensen et al., 2016).
evidence: This is based on previous work from the authors' lab supported by citation.

claim: RAB-28 is significantly overrepresented in a C. elegans EVN transcriptome.
source: An EV-related function for RAB-28 is also suggested by its significant overrepresentation in a C. elegans EVN transcriptome (Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is based on transcriptome data from previous work supported by citation.

claim: GFP-RAB-28Q95L mislocalization in the amphid and phasmid cilia of bbs-5(gk507) worms is indistinguishable from bbs-8(nx77) mutants; GFP signals are diffused throughout the neurons, with no detectable PCM enrichment or IFT movement.
source: We found that GFP-RAB-28Q95L mislocalization in the amphid and phasmid cilia of bbs-5(gk507) worms is indistinguishable from bbs-8(nx77) mutants; GFP signals are diffused throughout the neurons, with no detectable PCM enrichment or IFT movement (Figure 1, enhanced contrast images and expressivity shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and C).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1.

claim: arl-6(ok3472) mutants display a weaker phenotype, with modestly reduced levels of RAB-28 at the PCM and a diffuse dendritic localization.
source: By contrast, arl-6(ok3472) mutants display a weaker phenotype, with modestly reduced levels of RAB-28 at the PCM and a diffuse dendritic localization (Figure 1).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1.

claim: In arl-6 phasmid cilia, the frequency of GFP-RAB-28Q95L- positive IFT trains is increased twofold.
source: Also, in arl-6 phasmid cilia, the frequency of GFP-RAB-28Q95L- positive IFT trains is increased twofold (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and Video 1).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by quantitative microscopy data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: A complete and properly regulated BBSome is required for normal targeting and retention of RAB-28 to the PCM.
source: These data indicate that a complete and properly regulated BBSome is required for normal targeting and retention of RAB-28 to the PCM and that ARL-6 inhibits RAB-28 association with IFT trains, at least in amphid and phasmid neurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on RAB-28 localization in BBSome mutants.

claim: ARL-6 inhibits RAB-28 association with IFT trains, at least in amphid and phasmid neurons.
source: These data indicate that a complete and properly regulated BBSome is required for normal targeting and retention of RAB-28 to the PCM and that ARL-6 inhibits RAB-28 association with IFT trains, at least in amphid and phasmid neurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing increased IFT frequency in arl-6 mutants.

claim: The PCM localization of GFP-RAB-28Q95L remains intact in pdl-1(gk157) and arl-3(1703) null mutants, but the reporter's IFT motility is completely lost.
source: We found that whilst the PCM localization of GFP-RAB-28Q95L remains intact, the reporter's IFT motility is completely lost in pdl-1(gk157) and arl-3(1703) null mutants (Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1.

claim: PDL-1 is required for RAB-28 association with IFT trains in amphid and phasmid neurons, although it is dispensable for RAB-28 targeting to the PCM of these cells.
source: Thus, like the BBSome, the lipidated protein shuttle PDL-1 is also required for RAB-28 association with IFT trains in amphid and phasmid neurons, although it is dispensable for RAB-28 targeting to the PCM of these cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on RAB-28 localization in pdl-1 mutants.

claim: In pdl-1(gk157);arl-6(ok3472) worms, the reduced GFP::RAB-28Q95L PCM localization phenocopies that of the arl-6(ok3472) single mutant.
source: Similarly, in pdl-1(gk157);arl-6(ok3472) worms, the reduced GFP::RAB-28Q95L PCM localization phenocopies that of the arl-6(ok3472) single mutant, although there are additional diffuse signals in the cilium and distal dendrite (Figure 1).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from double mutant analysis supported by microscopy data.

claim: pdl-1 loss strongly suppresses the increased IFT frequency phenotype associated with arl-6 disruption.
source: With regard to RAB-28's IFT behavior phenotype, pdl-1 loss strongly suppresses the increased IFT frequency phenotype associated with arl-6 disruption, further supporting the critical role of PDL-1 in regulating RAB-28 loading onto IFT trains (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,C and Video 1).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from double mutant analysis supported by quantitative microscopy data.

claim: arl-6 and pdl-1 mutations are mutually suppressive, consistent with an opposing relationship in regulating the formation of RAB-28-positive IFT trains.
source: Since detectable IFT was never observed in the pdl-1(gk157) single mutant, the latter suggests that arl-6 and pdl-1 mutations are mutually suppressive, consistent with an opposing relationship in regulating the formation of RAB-28-positive IFT trains.
evidence: This is a genetic interpretation based on the double mutant analysis data.

claim: Activated RAB-28 is initially targeted to the PCM by the BBSome, and to a lesser extent ARL-6, and subsequently solubilized by PDL-1 for loading onto IFT trains, a step inhibited by ARL-6 in amphid and phasmid neurons.
source: Taken together, these data reveal a ciliary trafficking pathway in amphid and phasmid neurons whereby activated RAB-28 is initially targeted to the PCM by the BBSome, and to a lesser extent ARL-6, and subsequently solubilized by PDL-1 for loading onto IFT trains, a step inhibited by ARL-6 (summarized in Figure 1 schematic).
evidence: This is a model synthesized from the experimental data on RAB-28 localization in various mutants.

claim: There are 27 classified EVNs in C. elegans that include six IL2 head neurons of males and hermaphrodites and twenty one male-specific neurons (four CEM head neurons; 16 RnB tail ray neurons; one HOB tail hook neuron).
source: There are 27 classified EVNs in C. elegans that include six IL2 head neurons of males and hermaphrodites and twenty one male-specific neurons (four CEM head neurons; 16 RnB tail ray neurons; one HOB tail hook neuron) (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a statement about C. elegans anatomy based on previous work and confirmed by expression data in Figure 2A.

claim: rab-28 is expressed in the IL2 neurons present in both males and hermaphrodites, as well as all 21 male-specific EVNs.
source: rab-28 is expressed in the IL2 neurons present in both males and hermaphrodites, as well as all 21 male-specific EVNs (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by expression data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: RAB-28 is enriched at the PCM of CEM and RnB neurons.
source: Like amphid and phasmid channel neurons, RAB-28 is enriched at the PCM of CEM and RnB neurons (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Unlike amphid and phasmid cells, a pool of RAB-28 also occurs within the distal ends of the CEM and ray RnB cilia.
source: However, unlike amphid and phasmid cells, a pool of RAB-28 also occurs within the distal ends of the CEM and ray RnB cilia (see arrowheads in Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Moving RAB-28-positive IFT particles were rarely detected in CEM and RnB cilia.
source: Moving RAB-28-positive IFT particles were rarely detected in CEM and RnB cilia (Figure 2C and Video 2), consistent with our previous report showing that IFT in CEM cilia is less frequent than in amphid cilia (Morsci and Barr, 2011).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2C and Video 2.

claim: Almost all detectable RAB-28-positive IFT trains in male EVN cilia move in the retrograde direction.
source: Interestingly, almost all detectable RAB-28-positive IFT trains in male EVN cilia move in the retrograde direction (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: RAB-28 is not an EV cargo.
source: We did not observe RAB-28 in environmentally-released EVs, indicating that RAB-28 is not an EV cargo.
evidence: This is a negative finding from microscopy observations.

claim: GFP::RAB-28Q95L PCM localization was absent in bbs-5(gk507) and bbs-8(nx77) males in EVN cilia.
source: In EVN cilia, GFP::RAB-28Q95L PCM localization was absent in bbs-5(gk507) and bbs-8(nx77) males, whilst reduced in arl-6(ok3472) and pdl-1(gk157) males (Figure 2B), similar to phenotypes observed in the amphid and phasmid channel neuronal cilia (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: GFP::RAB-28Q95L PCM localization was reduced in arl-6(ok3472) and pdl-1(gk157) males in EVN cilia.
source: In EVN cilia, GFP::RAB-28Q95L PCM localization was absent in bbs-5(gk507) and bbs-8(nx77) males, whilst reduced in arl-6(ok3472) and pdl-1(gk157) males (Figure 2B), similar to phenotypes observed in the amphid and phasmid channel neuronal cilia (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The distal pool of RAB-28 in CEM and RnB cilia was reduced or absent in bbs-5, bbs-8, arl-6, and pdl-1 mutants.
source: Also, the distal pool of RAB-28 in CEM and RnB cilia was reduced or absent in all of these mutants (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: IFT movement of RAB-28Q95L was absent in bbs-5(gk507), bbs-8(nx77) and pdl-1(gk157) mutant EVN cilia.
source: Like in amphid and phasmid neurons, IFT movement of RAB-28Q95L was also absent in bbs-5(gk507), bbs-8(nx77) and pdl-1(gk157) mutant EVN cilia.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from microscopy observations.

claim: RAB-28Q95L IFT movement was not detectable in the EVN cilia of arl-6(ok3472) males, which is in striking contrast to the increased frequency of RAB-28-positive IFT trains in amphid and phasmid neurons.
source: Surprisingly, RAB-28Q95L IFT movement was also not detectable in the EVN cilia of arl-6(ok3472) males, which is in striking contrast to the increased frequency of RAB-28-positive IFT trains in amphid and phasmid neurons (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding highlighting cell-type specific differences.

claim: In pdl-1(gk157);arl-6(ok3472) double mutant EVNs, GFP::RAB-28Q95L is diffusely localized in the cytoplasm, with no PCM enrichment.
source: Analysis of pdl-1(gk157);arl-6(ok3472) double mutant EVNs revealed that GFP::RAB-28Q95L is diffusely localized in the cytoplasm, with no PCM enrichment (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from double mutant analysis supported by microscopy data.

claim: pdl-1 and arl-6 demonstrate an additive genetic relationship in targeting RAB-28 to EVN cilia, which is in contrast to that of amphid and phasmid neurons where the relationship is suppressive.
source: Thus, pdl-1 and arl-6 demonstrate an additive genetic relationship in targeting RAB-28 to EVN cilia, which is in contrast to that of amphid and phasmid neurons where the relationship is suppressive.
evidence: This is a genetic interpretation based on the double mutant analysis data showing cell-type specific differences.

claim: bbs-5(gk507) and bbs-8(nx77) mutant hermaphrodites abnormally accumulate electron dense matrix filled vesicles in the sheath cell process similar to RAB-28T26N-overexpressing worms.
source: We found that bbs-5(gk507) and bbs-8(nx77) mutant hermaphrodites abnormally accumulate electron dense matrix filled vesicles in the sheath cell process similar to RAB-28T26N-overexpressing worms, although sometimes at higher levels (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by TEM data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: bbs-5(gk507) and bbs-8(nx77) mutant hermaphrodites consistently exhibit highly distended amphid compartments, 2–3 times the size of WT, although with much darker staining of the extracellular matrix (ECM).
source: Additionally, much like hermaphrodites overexpressing RAB-28Q95L (GTP-preferring) (Jensen et al., 2016), bbs-5(gk507) and bbs-8(nx77) mutant hermaphrodites consistently exhibit highly distended amphid compartments,2–3 times the size of WT,although with much darker staining of the extracellular matrix (ECM) (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by TEM data shown in Figure 3A,B.

claim: At the level of the ciliary middle segments and transition zones, where the compartment is most enlarged, bbs-5(gk507) and bbs-8(nx77) mutant compartments each contain 11 ciliary axonemes, instead of the usual 10.
source: Also, at the level of the ciliary middle segments and transition zones, where the compartment is most enlarged, bbs-5(gk507) and bbs-8(nx77) mutant compartments each contain 11 ciliary axonemes, instead of the usual 10 (Figure 3B,C).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by TEM data shown in Figure 3B,C.

claim: In arl-6(ok3472) mutant, whilst there are electron dense deposits in the sheath cell at the ciliary middle segment, transition zone and PCMC levels of the amphid sensory organ, compartment size and ECM density are normal.
source: A weaker phenotype was observed in the arl-6(ok3472) mutant; whilst there are electron dense deposits in the sheath cell at the ciliary middle segment, transition zone and PCMC levels of the amphid sensory organ, compartment size and ECM density are normal (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by TEM data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Disruption of the BBSome, or ARL-6 to a lesser extent, phenocopies the amphid sensory organ and sheath cell defects observed in rab-28-disrupted worms.
source: Together, these data show that disruption of the BBSome, or ARL-6 to a lesser extent, phenocopies the amphid sensory organ and sheath cell defects observed in rab-28-disrupted worms (overexpressing RAB-28T26N or RAB-28Q95L).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing TEM data across different mutants.

claim: C. elegans BBS genes are expressed exclusively in ciliated neurons.
source: As with rab-28, C. elegans BBS genes are expressed exclusively in ciliated neurons (Ansley et al., 2003; Fan et al., 2004), indicating that their effects on the amphid sheath cell are also likely due to cell non-autonomous functions.
evidence: This is established knowledge about BBS gene expression supported by citations.

claim: The effects of BBS genes on the amphid sheath cell are likely due to cell non-autonomous functions.
source: As with rab-28, C. elegans BBS genes are expressed exclusively in ciliated neurons (Ansley et al., 2003; Fan et al., 2004), indicating that their effects on the amphid sheath cell are also likely due to cell non-autonomous functions.
evidence: This is an inference based on the expression pattern of BBS genes and the observed sheath cell phenotypes.

claim: In the amphids, the BBSome, ARL-6 and RAB-28 function together in a common cell non-autonomous pathway that regulates sensory organ size.
source: Thus, in the amphids, the BBSome, ARL-6 and RAB-28 function together in a common cell non-autonomous pathway that regulates sensory organ size.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the phenotypic similarities between rab-28 and BBSome mutants.

claim: In rab-28(tm2636) mutant males, total PKD-2::GFP levels at the CEM ciliary region from the PCMC to the tip are similar to control.
source: In rab-28(tm2636) mutant males, total PKD-2::GFP levels at the CEM ciliary region from the PCMC to the tip are similar to control (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by quantitative microscopy data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: rab-28(tm2636) mutants display abnormally high PKD-2::GFP levels at more distal parts of the CEM cilium region, indicating a ciliary localization defective (Cil) phenotype.
source: However, fluorescence intensity measurement analyses revealed a subtle yet consistent change in the pattern of PKD-2::GFP distribution in rab-28(tm2636) males indicating a ciliary localization defective (Cil) phenotype. Specifically, unlike control animals where PKD-2::GFP is most intense at the PCMC region of the CEM cilium, rab-28(tm2636) mutants display abnormally high PKD-2::GFP levels at more distal parts of the CEM cilium region (Figure 4B,C).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by quantitative microscopy data shown in Figure 4B,C.

claim: Control and rab-28(tm2636) males release similar numbers of PKD-2::GFP-labeled EVs.
source: We found that control and rab-28(tm2636) males release similar numbers of PKD-2::GFP-labeled EVs, ruling out a function for RAB-28 in environmental EV release of PKD-2 and suggesting a possible defect whereby EV shedding into the sensory organ lumen is abnormally upregulated (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by quantitative microscopy data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: RAB-28 is not required for the release of PKD-2-positive EVs into the environment.
source: We found that control and rab-28(tm2636) males release similar numbers of PKD-2::GFP-labeled EVs, ruling out a function for RAB-28 in environmental EV release of PKD-2 and suggesting a possible defect whereby EV shedding into the sensory organ lumen is abnormally upregulated (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the EV release quantification data.

claim: The rab-28(tm2636) cephalic sensory organ abnormally accumulates large amounts of CIL-7::GFP in ciliary regions.
source: In contrast to the relatively subtle PKD-2::GFP Cil phenotype, the rab-28(tm2636) cephalic sensory organ abnormally accumulates large amounts of CIL-7::GFP in ciliary regions (Figure 4F–H).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4F–H.

claim: A similar strong Cil phenotype was also observed in rab-28(gk1040) worms.
source: A similar strong Cil phenotype was also observed in rab-28(gk1040) worms (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Wild-type and rab-28(tm2636) males release similar numbers of CIL-7::GFP-containing EVs in mounting media.
source: Wild-type and rab-28(tm2636) males release similar numbers of CIL-7::GFP-containing EVs in mounting media (Figure 4I and Figure 4—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by quantitative microscopy data.

claim: RAB-28 regulates the abundance and distribution of ciliary proteins expressed in the EV-releasing CEM neurons.
source: These results indicate a role for RAB-28 in regulating the abundance and distribution of ciliary proteins expressed in the EV-releasing CEM neurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the PKD-2 and CIL-7 localization data in rab-28 mutants.

claim: RAB-28 is not required for the release of CIL-7-positive EVs into the environment.
source: Our data also indicate that RAB-28 is not required for the release of PKD-2- and CIL-7-positive EVs into the environment.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the EV release quantification data.

claim: bbs-8(nx77) and, to a lesser extent, arl-6(ok3472) mutants show Cil defects, with the ciliary EV marker CIL-7::GFP accumulating at the PCMC and around the axonemal region of CEM cilia.
source: Similar to rab-28 mutants, we found Cil defects in bbs-8(nx77) and, to a lesser extent, arl-6(ok3472) mutants, with the ciliary EV marker CIL-7::GFP accumulating at the PCMC and around the axonemal region of CEM cilia (Figure 4J–L).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4J–L.

claim: pdl-1(gk157) mutants show no gross CIL-7 localization defects.
source: In contrast, pdl-1(gk157) mutants show no gross CIL-7 localization defects (Figure 4J,L).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4J,L.

claim: bbs-8(nx77), arl-6(ok372) and pdl-1(gk157) mutant males show no defect in the number of CIL-7-labeled EVs released into the media.
source: Similar to rab-28 mutant males, we found no defect in the number of CIL-7-labeled EVs released into the media by bbs-8(nx77), arl-6(ok372) and pdl-1(gk157) mutant males (Figure 4M,N).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by quantitative microscopy data shown in Figure 4M,N.

claim: RAB-28, BBS-8 and ARL-6, but not PDL-1, regulate the localization and levels of EV markers in the ciliated sensory organs.
source: Together, these data indicate that RAB-28, BBS-8 and ARL-6, but not PDL-1, regulate the localization and levels of EV markers in the ciliated sensory organs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the CIL-7 and PKD-2 localization data across different mutants.

claim: RAB-28, BBS-8 and ARL-6 do not regulate the release of EVs from the sensory organs into the external environment of the worm.
source: However, they do not regulate the release of EVs from the sensory organs into the external environment of the worm.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the EV release quantification data.

claim: In wild-type males, EVs are observed in the extracellular space of the cephalic sensory organ (ie. the lumen).
source: In wild-type males, EVs are observed in the extracellular space of the cephalic sensory organ (ie. the lumen) (Figure 5B,C and Video 3).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by TEM data shown in Figure 5B,C and Video 3.

claim: In wild-type males, EVs in the cephalic lumen are typically of low electron density and found predominantly in the proximal regions of the lumen, although a few occur in distal regions.
source: These EVs are typically of low electron density and found predominantly in the proximal regions of the lumen, although a few occur in distal regions (Figure 5B; Wang et al., 2014a; Silva et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by TEM data shown in Figure 5B and previous work.

claim: In rab-28(tm2636) male worms, the distal part of the cephalic lumen is enlarged and accumulates an excess of EVs.
source: In rab-28(tm2636) male worms, the distal part of the cephalic lumen is enlarged and accumulates an excess of EVs.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by TEM data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: rab-28 mutant EVs are smaller and more uniform in size, and sometimes more electron dense, possibly indicating a change in composition.
source: When compared with control counterparts, these rab-28 mutant EVs are smaller and more uniform in size, and sometimes more electron dense, possibly indicating a change in composition (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1B, Video 3).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by TEM data with speculative interpretation about composition.

claim: In proximal parts of the lumen, at the level of the CEP and CEM ciliary transition zones and PCMCs, rab-28(tm2636) mutants show increased incidence of electron dense EVs.
source: In proximal parts of the lumen, at the level of the CEP and CEM ciliary transition zones and PCMCs, we also observed increased incidence of electron dense EVs (Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C,E,F and Video 3).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by TEM data.

claim: RAB-28 loss disrupts the number and nature of EVs in the lumens of cephalic sensory organs.
source: Thus, RAB-28 loss disrupts the number and nature of EVs in the lumens of cephalic sensory organs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the TEM data on EVs in rab-28 mutants.

claim: The cephalic sensory organ and CEM ciliary tip in the rab-28(tm2636) mutant retains normal exposure to the environment.
source: Notably, electron tomographic analysis revealed that the cephalic sensory organ and CEM ciliary tip in the rab-28(tm2636) mutant retains normal exposure to the environment, indicating that pore blockage or a ciliogenesis defect is not the cause of EV accumulation in the distal lumen (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by electron tomography data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: rab-28(tm2636) worms retain the normal CEM ciliary axonemal AB tubule split that is important to EV release.
source: Also, rab-28(tm2636) worms retain the normal CEM ciliary axonemal AB tubule split that is important to EV release (Silva et al., 2017; O'Hagan et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding with reference to previous work on the importance of the AB tubule split.

claim: rab-28(tm2636) mutant males produce and shed excessive amounts of abnormally stained and sized EVs into the cephalic sensory organ.
source: We conclude from these data that rab-28(tm2636) mutant males produce and shed excessive amounts of abnormally stained and sized EVs into the cephalic sensory organ.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the TEM data on EVs in rab-28 mutants.

claim: RAB-28 regulates EV cargo sorting and production (biogenesis).
source: These data suggest that RAB-28 regulates EV cargo sorting and production (biogenesis) and that RAB-28 acts as a negative regulator of EV shedding without affecting environmental EV release.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the TEM and fluorescence microscopy data on EVs in rab-28 mutants.

claim: RAB-28 acts as a negative regulator of EV shedding without affecting environmental EV release.
source: These data suggest that RAB-28 regulates EV cargo sorting and production (biogenesis) and that RAB-28 acts as a negative regulator of EV shedding without affecting environmental EV release.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined TEM and fluorescence microscopy data.

claim: RAB-28 negatively regulates cephalic sensory compartment size.
source: Our findings also show that RAB-28 negatively regulates cephalic sensory compartment size, in agreement with what we previously reported for RAB-28 in the amphid organs (Jensen et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the TEM data showing enlarged cephalic lumen in rab-28 mutants.

claim: In bbs-8(nx77) male worms, the cephalic lumen is distended and filled throughout (ie, proximal and distal regions) with abnormally large numbers of EVs.
source: In bbs-8(nx77) male worms, the cephalic lumen is distended and filled throughout (ie, proximal and distal regions) with abnormally large numbers of EVs (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by TEM data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Compared with rab-28(tm2636) worms, the accumulated EVs in bbs-8(nx77) mutant lumens are more numerous, and more varied in size.
source: Compared with rab-28(tm2636) worms, the accumulated EVs in bbs-8(nx77) mutant lumens are more numerous, and more varied in size.
evidence: This is a comparative observation from TEM data.

claim: Electron dense matrix filled vesicles are observed within seventy five percent of bbs-8(nx77) mutant cephalic sheath glia.
source: We also observed electron dense matrix filled vesicles within seventy five percent of bbs-8(nx77) mutant cephalic sheath glia (Figure 5D), matching the amphid sheath cell phenotype in these worms (Figure 3).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by TEM data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The ultrastructure of bbs-8(nx77) mutant CEM cilia is grossly normal.
source: Similar to rab-28(tm2636) mutants, the ultrastructure of bbs-8(nx77) mutant CEM cilia is grossly normal.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from TEM observations.

claim: Like RAB-28, the BBSome also negatively regulates EV shedding in the cephalic organ and the size of the organ's lumen.
source: Thus, like RAB-28, the BBSome also negatively regulates EV shedding in the cephalic organ and the size of the organ's lumen.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the TEM data on EVs and lumen size in bbs-8 mutants.

claim: The differences in the severity of the EV phenotype in bbs-8(nx77) and rab-28(tm2636) mutants indicate a greater role for BBS-8 in EV regulation, possibly because the BBSome regulates the trafficking of multiple EV regulators and not just RAB-28.
source: The differences in the severity of the EV phenotype in bbs-8(nx77) and rab-28(tm2636) mutants, and in the appearance of EVs that accumulate in both these worms, indicate a greater role for BBS-8 in EV regulation, possibly because the BBSome regulates the trafficking of multiple EV regulators and not just RAB-28.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the comparative severity of phenotypes.

claim: Large accumulations of EVs are observed in the amphid lumen of male bbs-8(nx77) mutants.
source: In contrast, large accumulations of EVs are observed in the amphid lumen of male bbs-8(nx77) mutants (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by TEM data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: EVs in the amphid lumen of bbs-8(nx77) mutants are heterogeneous in size and appearance, and occur throughout the amphid sensory organ (proximal and distal regions).
source: These EVs are heterogeneous in size and appearance, and occur throughout the amphid sensory organ (proximal and distal regions) (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by TEM data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: BBS-8 suppresses abnormal amphid EV shedding in a RAB-28-independent manner.
source: We conclude that BBS-8 suppresses abnormal amphid EV shedding in a RAB-28-independent manner.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that bbs-8 but not rab-28 mutants show ectopic amphid EVs.

claim: The BBSome does not depend on RAB-28 for localization to phasmid cilia.
source: Our transport data here are in agreement with previous observations that the BBSome does not depend on RAB-28 for localization to phasmid cilia (Jensen et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a statement consistent with previous work supported by citation.

claim: The PCM is the primary membrane at which RAB-28 functions.
source: Taken together, our data suggest that the PCM is the primary membrane at which RAB-28 functions and that its levels at the PCM and ciliary membranes membrane are regulated by a combination of the BBSome, IFT, and lipidated protein transport machinery in a cell-specific manner.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the localization and trafficking data.

claim: RAB-28 levels at the PCM and ciliary membranes are regulated by a combination of the BBSome, IFT, and lipidated protein transport machinery in a cell-specific manner.
source: Taken together, our data suggest that the PCM is the primary membrane at which RAB-28 functions and that its levels at the PCM and ciliary membranes membrane are regulated by a combination of the BBSome, IFT, and lipidated protein transport machinery in a cell-specific manner.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the localization and trafficking data across different cell types and mutants.

claim: Rab28 localization to the outer segments of mouse photoreceptors is disrupted in Arl3 and Pde6d mutants.
source: This latter observation is in concordance with, and expands upon, previous reports that Rab28 localization to the outer segments of mouse photoreceptors is disrupted in Arl3 and Pde6d mutants (Hanke-Gogokhia et al., 2016; Ying et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous studies supported by citations.

claim: Rab28 is one of only two proteins known to undergo both IFT and lipidated protein transport, the other being INPP5E.
source: Rab28 is one of only two proteins known to undergo both IFT and lipidated protein transport, the other being INPP5E (Fansa et al., 2016; Kösling et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous studies supported by citations.

claim: For both Rab28 and INPP5E, PDE6D is required for initial ciliary import and IFT for subsequent transport within cilia and, presumably, exit.
source: In both cases, PDE6D is required for initial ciliary import and IFT for subsequent transport within cilia and, presumably, exit.
evidence: This is a general mechanism inferred from studies on both proteins.

claim: This may be a general mechanism for the ciliary targeting and distribution of lipidated proteins.
source: This may, therefore, be a general mechanism for the ciliary targeting and distribution of lipidated proteins.
evidence: This is a speculative generalization based on the observations for Rab28 and INPP5E.

claim: C. elegans RAB-28 could serve as a useful model for investigating the trafficking of ciliary lipidated proteins and crosstalk between IFT and lipidated protein transport.
source: Aside from its functional roles in cilia, C. elegans RAB-28 could serve as a useful model for investigating the trafficking of ciliary lipidated proteins and crosstalk between IFT and lipidated protein transport.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the utility of the C. elegans system.

claim: In male EVN cilia, a distinct pool of RAB-28 is present in the distal region, while the frequency of RAB-28Q95L IFT events is much lower than in phasmids.
source: Intriguingly, we observe cell-type specific differences in RAB-28 localization and targeting. In male EVN cilia, a distinct pool of RAB-28 is present in the distal region, while the frequency of RAB-28Q95L IFT events is much lower than in phasmids.
evidence: This is a summary of experimental findings showing cell-type specific differences.

claim: PDL-1/PDE6D is partially required for maintaining RAB-28 PCM levels in EVN cilia but not amphid/phasmid cilia.
source: Whilst the requirement for the BBSome in regulating RAB-28 PCM association and IFT behavior is identical in all analyzed ciliary subtypes, PDL-1/PDE6D is partially required for maintaining RAB-28 PCM levels in EVN cilia but not amphid/phasmid cilia.
evidence: This is a summary of experimental findings showing cell-type specific differences.

claim: Cell type-specific differences in RAB-28 ciliary trafficking correlate with distinctions in IFT and PCMC composition between amphid/phasmid and EVN cilia.
source: Indeed, cell type-specific differences in RAB-28 ciliary trafficking correlate with distinctions in IFT and PCMC composition between amphid/phasmid and EVN cilia (Morsci and Barr, 2011; Scheidel et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a correlation drawn between the observed differences and previous work on IFT and PCMC composition.

claim: EV release from the cephalic sensory organ lumen to the animal's external environment is not affected in rab-28 mutants.
source: Notably, EV release from the cephalic sensory organ lumen to the animal's external environment is not affected in rab-28 mutants, indicating that the accumulated EVs in the mutant sensory organs arise due to abnormalities in biogenesis and shedding at the ciliary base rather than environmental release.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the EV release quantification data.

claim: The accumulated EVs in rab-28 mutant sensory organs arise due to abnormalities in biogenesis and shedding at the ciliary base rather than environmental release.
source: Notably, EV release from the cephalic sensory organ lumen to the animal's external environment is not affected in rab-28 mutants, indicating that the accumulated EVs in the mutant sensory organs arise due to abnormalities in biogenesis and shedding at the ciliary base rather than environmental release.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined TEM and fluorescence microscopy data.

claim: Defective targeting of RAB-28 to EVN periciliary membranes, via mutation of the BBSome, elicits a similar EV accumulation phenotype.
source: We also show that defective targeting of RAB-28 to EVN periciliary membranes, via mutation of the BBSome, elicits a similar phenotype.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comparison of rab-28 and BBSome mutant phenotypes.

claim: RAB-28 and the BBSome are negative regulators of EV shedding at the ciliary base.
source: These findings indicate: (i) RAB-28 and the BBSome are negative regulators of EV shedding at the ciliary base, and (ii) the PCM may be the site of RAB-28's EV-related function.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on EV accumulation in mutants.

claim: The PCM may be the site of RAB-28's EV-related function.
source: These findings indicate: (i) RAB-28 and the BBSome are negative regulators of EV shedding at the ciliary base, and (ii) the PCM may be the site of RAB-28's EV-related function.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the localization and functional data.

claim: There is a tuneable system of EV regulation in EVNs that consists of transport regulators that control the levels and localization of EV regulators in cells and cilia.
source: Taken together, our data indicate the presence of a tuneable system of EV regulation in EVNs that consists of transport regulators that control the levels and localization of EV regulators in cells and cilia.
evidence: This is a model synthesized from the experimental data.

claim: The BBSome targets additional EV regulators, beyond RAB-28, to EVN cilia.
source: Since the prevalence, pattern, and extent of the EV phenotype is more severe in BBSome vs RAB-28 deficient worms, our data also suggests that the BBSome targets additional EV regulators, beyond RAB-28, to EVN cilia.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comparative severity of phenotypes.

claim: Mutants of KLP-6, CCPP-1, TTLL-11, TBA-6, and CIL-7 showed disruption of environmental EV release with an excessive EV accumulation within sensory organs.
source: Mutants of previously identified cilia-related EV regulators such as KLP-6, CCPP-1, TTLL-11, TBA-6, and CIL-7 showed disruption of environmental EV release with an excessive EV accumulation within sensory organs (Wang et al., 2015; Maguire et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2014a; O'Hagan et al., 2017; Silva et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous work supported by citations.

claim: rab-28 and bbs-8 mutants are EV ciliary base shedding, but not release defective, providing the very first evidence that EV shedding and release mechanisms are genetically separate.
source: Our data that rab-28 and bbs-8 mutants are EV ciliary base shedding, but not release defective provides the very first evidence that EV shedding and release mechanisms are genetically separate.
evidence: This is a novel conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing distinct phenotypes.

claim: The PCM is a major site of EV ciliary base shedding.
source: Our data is also consistent with the PCM being a major site of EV ciliary base shedding, although it cannot be ruled out that at least some of the EVs originate from other regions of the cilium or even the sheath and socket glial cells that surround the cilium (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the localization and functional data with some uncertainty.

claim: Both Rab28 and the BBSome have previously been associated with endosomal sorting and degradative processes in Trypanosomes and C. elegans.
source: Indeed, both Rab28 and the BBSome have previously been associated with endosomal sorting and degradative processes in Trypanosomes and C. elegans (Lumb et al., 2011; Xu et al., 2015; Langousis et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous studies supported by citations.

claim: Defective ciliary protein turnover in Rab28 or BBSome-disrupted worms would lead to a compensatory mechanism whereby receptors are removed from the ciliary/periciliary membrane via EV shedding.
source: In one model, defective ciliary protein turnover in Rab28 or BBSome-disrupted worms would lead to a compensatory mechanism whereby receptors are removed from the ciliary/periciliary membrane via EV shedding.
evidence: This is a speculative model proposed to explain the EV accumulation phenotype.

claim: This model is in agreement with the proposed mechanism for excess ciliary ectosome production in BBSome-depleted mammalian cells.
source: This model is in agreement with the proposed mechanism for excess ciliary ectosome production in BBSome-depleted mammalian cells (Nager et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a comparison to a previous study supported by citation.

claim: In the mouse retina, photoreceptor disc formation requires the suppression of EV release by the disk-specific protein peripherin.
source: For example, in the mouse retina, photoreceptor disc formation requires the suppression of EV release by the disk-specific protein peripherin (Salinas et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous work supported by citation.

claim: In peripherin-disrupted mice that display photoreceptor degeneration, the ectopic EVs that surround the photoreceptor can be considered as pathological.
source: Thus, in peripherin-disrupted mice that display photoreceptor degeneration, the ectopic EVs that surround the photoreceptor can be considered as pathological.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on previous work.

claim: Pathological EVs (ectosomes) are reported to be released from the tips of IMCD3 cells depleted of the BBSome.
source: Also, pathological EVs (ectosomes) are reported to be released from the tips of IMCD3 cells depleted of the BBSome (Nager et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous work supported by citation.

claim: The amphid sensory organ represents a simple model to identify mechanisms that regulate the formation of ectopic and pathological EVs.
source: Thus, like the photoreceptor and IMCD3 scenarios, where EV shedding is normally rare, the amphid sensory organ represents a simple model to identify mechanisms that regulate the formation of ectopic and pathological EVs.
evidence: This is a statement about the utility of the C. elegans amphid system as a model.

claim: bbs-8 and rab-28 mutants display expanded sensory organ lumens and abnormally large deposits of dense vesicular material in the sheath cytoplasm that surrounds the lumen.
source: Specifically, bbs-8 and rab-28 mutants display expanded sensory organ lumens and abnormally large deposits of dense vesicular material in the sheath cytoplasm that surrounds the lumen .
evidence: This is a summary of experimental findings from TEM data.

claim: Such deposits have been previously observed in ciliary mutants.
source: Such deposits have been previously observed in ciliary mutants (Perkins et al., 1986; Braunreiter et al., 2014; De Vore, 2018) and correspond to altered forms of matrix-filled vesicles (MFVs) that normally deliver membrane and ECM to the pore (Ward et al., 1975; Bacaj et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous studies supported by citations.

claim: The size and composition of the amphid sensory organ is thought to be critically dependent on exocytic and endocytic pathways in the sheath cell that control the amount of matrix and membrane deposited at, and retrieved from, the lumen.
source: Indeed, the size and composition of the amphid sensory organ is thought to be critically dependent on exocytic and endocytic pathways in the sheath cell that control the amount of matrix and membrane deposited at, and retrieved from, the lumen (Perens and Shaham, 2005; Singhvi and Shaham, 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous studies supported by citations.

claim: Signaling from amphid cilia has been proposed to regulate the localization of glial factors such as DAF-6 and LIT-1 that regulate the size of the sensory compartment/sensory organ.
source: Additionally, signaling from amphid cilia has been proposed to regulate the localization of glial factors such as DAF-6 and LIT-1 that regulate the size of the sensory compartment/sensory organ (Oikonomou et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous work supported by citation.

claim: RAB-28 and the BBSome coordinate sensory organ morphogenesis via signaling events that mediate neuronal-glial interactions.
source: Given these observations, we propose that RAB-28 and the BBSome coordinate sensory organ morphogenesis via signaling events that mediate neuronal-glial interactions (Figure 7; Table 1).
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the experimental data and previous knowledge.

claim: EV exchange between neurons and glia has been documented in vitro and in vivo.
source: Indeed, EV exchange between neurons and glia has been documented in vitro and in vivo (Lopez-Verrilli et al., 2013; Frühbeis et al., 2013; Fröhlich et al., 2014; Goncalves et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous studies supported by citations.

claim: The association of RAB28 and BBSome gene disruption with cone-rod dystrophy and retinitis pigmentosa raises the possibility that EV regulatory functions contribute to human retinal disease.
source: The association of RAB28 and BBSome gene disruption with cone-rod dystrophy (Roosing et al., 2013; Riveiro-Álvarez et al., 2015; Lee et al., 2017; Ying et al., 2018) and retinitis pigmentosa (Waters and Beales, 2011; Weihbrecht, 2017) raises the possibility that EV regulatory functions contribute to human retinal disease.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the association of these genes with human disease and the EV phenotypes observed.

claim: Suppression of ciliary EV release is a crucial step in the formation of the discs of the outer segments (OS) of photoreceptors.
source: As mentioned above, suppression of ciliary EV release is a crucial step in the formation of the discs of the outer segments (OS) of photoreceptors (Salinas et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous work supported by citation.

claim: 10% of the OS undergoes a daily renewal process that involves disc shedding and phagocytosis by neighboring retinal pigmented epithelium (RPE) cells.
source: 10% of the OS undergoes a daily renewal process that involves disc shedding and phagocytosis by neighboring retinal pigmented epithelium (RPE) cells (Kevany and Palczewski, 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge about photoreceptor biology supported by citation.

claim: The observation of EV shedding defects in C. elegans rab-28 and bbs-8 gene mutants, together with reduced disc shedding and/or phagocytosis reported in Rab28 knockout mice, allows us to propose that OS disc and EV shedding processes may involve a shared Rab28 mechanism.
source: Nonetheless, our observation of EV shedding defects in C. elegans rab-28 and bbs-8 gene mutants, together with reduced disc shedding and/or phagocytosis reported in Rab28 knockout mice (Ying et al., 2018), allows us to propose that OS disc and EV shedding processes may involve a shared Rab28 mechanism.
evidence: This is a speculative proposal based on the C. elegans data and mouse data from previous work.

claim: Rab28 positively regulates mouse OS shedding but negatively regulates C. elegans EV shedding.
source: However, the precise nature of this mechanism is unclear given that Rab28 positively regulates mouse OS shedding but negatively regulates C. elegans EV shedding.
evidence: This is a statement highlighting the apparent contradiction between mouse and C. elegans data.

claim: Bbs8 mutant mice exhibit defects in OS morphogenesis, including disorganized discs and a shorter OS.
source: Furthermore, although Bbs8 mutant mice exhibit defects in OS morphogenesis, including disorganized discs and a shorter OS (Hsu et al., 2017), it remains to be determined if the BBSome functions in disc shedding.
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous work supported by citation.

claim: Molecules regulating ciliary EV biogenesis and shedding such as those identified in C. elegans sensory organs may provide insight into the molecular mechanisms underpinning OS formation and/or disc shedding.
source: Molecules regulating ciliary EV biogenesis and shedding such as those identified in C. elegans sensory organs may provide insight into the molecular mechanisms underpinning OS formation and/or disc shedding.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential translational relevance of the findings.

claim: Rab28 is only the second Rab family member shown to have a role in cilia-related EV biogenesis, the other being IFT27/Rabl4.
source: Rab28 is only the second Rab family member shown to have a role in cilia-related EV biogenesis, the other being IFT27/Rabl4 (Nager et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a statement about the novelty of the finding supported by citation.

claim: Neither Rab28 nor IFT27/Rabl4 is associated with EV generation in other contexts.
source: Neither is associated with EV generation in other contexts.
evidence: This is a statement about the specificity of these Rabs to ciliary EV biogenesis.

claim: The cilium may use some unique EV-regulators, enabling the cilium to modulate its EV output independently of the rest of the plasma membrane.
source: Therefore, the cilium may use some unique EV-regulators, enabling the cilium to modulate its EV output independently of the rest of the plasma membrane.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the specificity of Rab28 and IFT27 to ciliary EV biogenesis.

claim: Previous work identified that EV biogenesis, shedding and release is normal in ESCRT pathway mutants.
source: Our previous work identified that EV biogenesis, shedding and release is normal in ESCRT pathway mutants (Wang et al., 2014b), and multivesicular bodies are not observed in the region of the ciliary base by TEM.
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous work supported by citation.

claim: Multivesicular bodies are not observed in the region of the ciliary base by TEM.
source: Our previous work identified that EV biogenesis, shedding and release is normal in ESCRT pathway mutants (Wang et al., 2014b), and multivesicular bodies are not observed in the region of the ciliary base by TEM.
evidence: This is a primary experimental observation from TEM data.

claim: The genetic and electron microscopy data are consistent with these small ciliary EVs (average diameter 104.7 ± 46.7 nm) not being exosomes but ectosomes/microvesicles instead.
source: Hence, our genetic and electron microscopy data are consistent with these small ciliary EVs (average diameter 104.7 ± 46.7 nm) not being exosomes but ectosomes/microvesicles instead.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the genetic and TEM data.

claim: Omega-shaped vesicle budding from the ciliary base has been observed.
source: This conclusion is also supported by our observation of omega-shaped vesicle budding from the ciliary base (Wang et al., 2014b; Silva et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a primary experimental observation from previous work supported by citations.
